candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

Everyday I use qualities such as patience, mildness, tolerance and love in what I do.  These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Intake Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy.  I am passionate about mental health and particularly enjoy working with adolescents. I believe that every young person has a unique way of understanding the world, and one of the things I value most about working with them is that I learn so much from each individual and their thought process. I find it meaningful to understand their perspectives, recognize their needs, and contribute to an environment where they feel heard, respected, and supported; it matter to me the most to provide a safe space for each and everyone of them.

Through my psychology practicums, I have gained experience conducting psychological assessments with adolescents, administering and interpreting psychological tests, and participating in interventions focused on adolescent development, family unity, and violence prevention. I have also worked with children who have experienced abandonment or violence, which has strengthened my empathy and taught me the importance of approaching sensitive situations with patience, care, and professionalism.

I consider myself a highly empathetic, adaptable, and resourceful person. I learn quickly, think critically, and enjoy finding practical solutions when challenges arise. I understand that supporting adolescents and their families involves not only compassion but also organization, clear communication, and attention to detail. I am comfortable working with Zoom and digital tools, and I would be confident managing virtual interactions while helping families navigate the intake process and ensuring that information is communicated accurately to the appropriate team members.

As a native Spanish speaker with C1-level English proficiency, I can communicate effectively with families in both languages and help create a more accessible and welcoming experience. I would be excited to contribute my psychological background, interpersonal skills, and genuine interest in adolescent well-being to AWA's mission of supporting young people and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, motivation, and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Mariana Ochoa Ortiz

education.summary: I am currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Psychology at Universidad Iberoamericana in Mexico City. My academic training has provided me with a strong foundation in psychological assessment, human development, mental health, and individual and group interventions. Through coursework and practical experiences, I have developed critical thinking, empathy, and communication skills, with a particular interest in adolescent development and emotional well-being. I am eager to apply my knowledge to support individuals and families while continuing to grow professionally.

I completed a semester abroad at Concordia University in Montreal, Canada, from January to May 2026, as part of my Psychology degree at Universidad Iberoamericana. This experience strengthened my adaptability, independence, cross-cultural communication, and ability to navigate new environments. Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. With more than three years of experience in healthcare, care coordination, and social services, along with my ongoing Master of Social Work studies and clinical internship at Boca Recovery Center, I bring a strong foundation in patient advocacy, behavioral health support, resource navigation, and multidisciplinary collaboration.

Throughout my career, I have supported individuals and families navigating complex healthcare needs, behavioral health challenges, and difficult life transitions. My experience includes conducting assessments, developing individualized care plans, coordinating services, documenting clinical information, and helping individuals connect with resources that support their well-being. At Boca Recovery Center, I have gained additional clinical experience working with individuals affected by substance use disorders, participating in therapeutic groups, supporting recovery-oriented goals, and developing my skills in motivational interviewing and therapeutic communication.

What draws me to AWA is your commitment to looking beyond adolescents’ behaviors to understand the emotions, experiences, and challenges behind them. I believe every young person deserves to feel heard, respected, and supported without judgment. I am passionate about helping adolescents and families navigate difficult circumstances while building trust, strengthening coping skills, and recognizing their potential for growth and recovery.

As a trilingual professional fluent in English, Portuguese, and Spanish, I also value the opportunity to support diverse populations and help families feel understood throughout their care journey. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, compassion, adaptability, and commitment to AWA’s mission while continuing to grow professionally within a collaborative behavioral health team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and dedication to supporting individuals and families could contribute to the work of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,  
Ruth De Azevedo

candidates.cover_letter:
Throughout my career, I have had the privilege of working with students from a variety of backgrounds and with a wide range of academic, behavioral, and emotional needs. My experience in special education has shaped not only the professional I am today, but also the way I view the importance of creating safe spaces for young people who may be navigating some of the most difficult seasons of their lives.

Much of my career has been dedicated to special education, and I currently work in a modified setting supporting high school students. I have also worked with middle and high school students in both Emotional or Behavioral Disabilities (EBD) and Intellectual Disabilities (IND) settings. These experiences have taught me that working with adolescents requires much more than structure and routine. It requires understanding that every young person has a story and recognizing that behavior can be a form of communication. Some of the most meaningful moments in my career have come from seeing a student make progress that others may have once thought was out of reach.

My commitment to young people extends beyond the classroom. I have worked with students throughout different parts of Miami, from South Miami to Overtown, and when I lived closer to the area, I also volunteered at the Overtown Youth Center. Those experiences helped reinforce how much a young person's environment and access to caring adults can influence their path. That belief is a major reason this opportunity resonates with me.

While my professional background is rooted in education, I have also developed valuable operational and organizational skills through my previous experience with Wix and Publix. At Publix, I gained hands-on experience helping manage front-of-house operations, coordinating with leadership, and working collaboratively on staff scheduling and coverage. I learned the importance of anticipating needs, communicating clearly, adjusting to unexpected changes, and ensuring that the people and resources around me were in the right place for the day to run successfully. Combined with my experience in education, behavioral support, documentation, and student safety, these skills have prepared me to contribute to a role that requires both compassion and strong operational judgment.

As I consider this next chapter in my career, I am looking for a path that allows me to continue making a meaningful difference while also being intentional about my future and my responsibilities to my family. My decision to explore a career transition is not a reflection of losing my passion for education or for working with young people. Rather, it comes from a desire to build on what I have learned, grow into new leadership opportunities, and continue serving adolescents and families in a different capacity. I hope to bring the perspective of an educator who understands that the people behind the daily operations matter just as much as the systems that keep a program running..

It would be an honor to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's mission and to help create an environment where adolescents feel supported and staff feel equipped to do their best work. Thank you for considering my application and for the work your organization does for young people and families throughout South Florida. I would welcome the opportunity to share more about my experience and how I hope to contribute to your team.

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., NCC
Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI)
South Florida | Hallandale Beach

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern
+1 (561) 289-5680 | paula@lm2services.com

candidates.cover_letter:
Hello,

I'm so excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position! With my experience supporting people facing behavioral health challenges, my background in customer service and caregiving, and my ongoing studies in Social Work at Olympic College, I believe I would be a good asset to your team!

During my time at Kitsap Mental Health Services, I developed an understanding of the importance of compassionate, respectful, trauma-informed, and person-centered support. Working with people of various ages who were experiencing homelessness, substance use challenges, and varying mental health concerns taught me the importance of treating everyone with dignity, communicating effectively, and meeting people where they are in their lives. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can feel overwhelming, intimidating, or even hopeless, and I believe that having someone who is patient, understanding, and nonjudgmental can make a meaningful difference in someone's willingness to seek help.

In my current role as a Before and After School Teacher with Champions, I continue to strengthen my communication, organization, patience, and problem-solving skills. Working in a busy environment requires me to manage competing priorities, remain attentive to individual needs, communicate professionally with my team and parents, and maintain a safe and supportive environment. My additional experience in childcare, senior care, and retail has helped me develop a versatile skill set that includes customer service, adaptability, teamwork, and the ability to interact with people from different backgrounds.

I'm interested in this position because it combines my interest in behavioral health and social services with administrative coordination and client communication, which are areas I've been actively looking to pursue in my career. I'd welcome the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the admissions process, answer questions about available treatment options, coordinate intake appointments, and make the process of accessing care feel a little less intimidating. I recognize the importance of clear communication, accurate documentation, confidentiality, and consistent follow-up, especially when working with people who may already be experiencing difficult circumstances. I'm also eager to continue learning and developing my skills in behavioral health admissions and care coordination!

As someone who's pursuing an education in Social Work, I'm passionate about helping people access the support they need and believe that everyone deserves to be treated with compassion and respect, regardless of their circumstances. I would be excited to bring that perspective, along with my existing experience and willingness to learn, to your team.

Thank you so much for your time and consideration! I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and commitment to supporting individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges would make me a valuable addition to your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your work in helping people take the first steps toward recovery and a healthier future!

Thank you again,

Kayla Martin

I am writing to express my interest in the Admissions Coordinator position. I am excited about the opportunity to combine my strong organizational, communication, and customer service skills with my passion for helping individuals and families navigate the recovery process.

As an Admissions Coordinator, I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, and respect. I am committed to creating a welcoming and supportive experience for clients and their loved ones during what is often an emotional and uncertain time.
Throughout my professional experience, I have developed strong skills in client communication, scheduling, MANDT training, Peer Support training, and coordinating services. I am comfortable handling sensitive and confidential information, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring that each individual receives timely and compassionate help. My ability to remain calm under pressure, actively listen, and build trust allows me to effectively support people from many different backgrounds.
I am particularly drawn to your organization because of its commitment to transforming lives through addiction treatment and recovery support. I believe that every person deserves the opportunity to heal, and I would be honored to contribute to a team dedicated to making a positive difference in the lives of clients and their families.
I am eager to bring my dedication, strong work ethic, and people-centered approach to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my skills and enthusiasm can contribute to the continued success of your treatment center.

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with your organization. With my background in healthcare, medical coordination, patient communication, and supporting individuals with diverse needs, I believe I would be a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my experience as a Cardiology Medical Assistant, Medical Liaison, and Direct Support Professional, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills. My responsibilities have included coordinating appointments, communicating medical information, maintaining confidential records, assisting with healthcare needs, and working collaboratively with medical professionals to ensure individuals receive appropriate care and support.

I understand that seeking treatment for substance use can be a difficult and vulnerable time for individuals and their families. I believe that approaching each person with compassion, patience, professionalism, and without judgment is essential to helping them feel comfortable taking the first step toward recovery. I would welcome the opportunity to use my healthcare experience and communication skills to help individuals navigate the admissions process and connect with the services they need.

I am also pursuing my education in nursing, which continues to strengthen my understanding of patient-centered care, advocacy, and the importance of treating every individual with dignity and respect. I am eager to continue growing professionally while contributing to an organization dedicated to helping people improve their health and quality of life.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your organization.

Sincerely,
Darian Druker

Sincerely,

Wynter Lapila

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Mental Health position at Principles Recovery Center. With more than three years of experience in human services and behavioral health, including direct work with adults experiencing substance use disorders and coordination of outpatient treatment referrals, I would bring compassionate communication, organized follow-through, and a strong understanding of barriers to care to your admissions team.

In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Practitioner with Georgia HOPE, I assess client and family needs, explain treatment expectations, coordinate services with providers and community partners, and maintain detailed electronic health records. I have supported adults experiencing substance use disorders as well as families affected by substance use, helping connect them with appropriate treatment resources. This work has strengthened my ability to discuss sensitive concerns without judgment, build trust, and guide people through unfamiliar care processes.

Previously, as a Family Support Specialist, I managed referrals and ongoing communication with families, DFCS, and community providers. Across both roles, I have learned the importance of timely follow-up, accurate documentation, and clear coordination when individuals are seeking support. I am comfortable managing competing priorities independently while keeping clients informed and engaged.

I hold a Bachelor of Arts in Human Services with a focus in Child and Family Welfare and am pursuing a Master of Science in Criminal Justice with a focus in Forensic Psychology. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience and client-centered approach to Principles Recovery Center and help prospective clients take the next step toward treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Joshua Kestner
Lancaster, CA

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator–Mental Health position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. My background in behavioral health leadership, case management, and substance use treatment has prepared me to communicate compassionately with people seeking support and help them navigate the next steps toward care.

My experience includes case management at New Vision Wellness, serving as Lead Tech at Desert Paradise Detox and Rehab, and working as a Substance Abuse Tech at New Life Recovery Center. These roles have reinforced the importance of listening carefully, maintaining professional boundaries, and communicating clearly with clients and treatment teams. I understand that a person’s first interaction with a program can influence whether they feel comfortable moving forward.

I would bring a calm, respectful approach to conversations with adolescents and their families. Seeking mental health treatment can feel overwhelming, especially for parents concerned about their child’s well-being. My approach would be to listen without judgment, explain the admissions process clearly, and coordinate with clinical staff so families receive accurate information and appropriate guidance.

Along with my direct service experience, my behavioral health leadership background has strengthened my sense of accountability and understanding of program operations. I value confidentiality, accurate documentation, consistent follow-through, and teamwork. I would apply these priorities to responding to inquiries, coordinating appointments, and supporting a smooth transition into services.

I am pursuing studies in Behavioral Health Sciences, and my long-term goal is to work with youth and families. This opportunity aligns closely with that goal and would allow me to contribute my experience while continuing to grow professionally.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and commitment to compassionate service could support Adolescent Wellness Academy’s admissions team.

Sincerely,
Joshua Kestner

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Mental Health position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over two years of experience in behavioral health and substance use recovery services, along with my education in Human Services and Counseling, I believe I would be a strong addition to your admissions team.

I currently work for Kentucky River Community Care (KRCC) through the Restore Hope program, where I serve as a Peer Support Specialist and Data Collector. My responsibilities include conducting client assessments, coordinating referrals, maintaining accurate documentation, completing follow-ups, and assisting individuals and families in accessing mental health and substance use treatment services. I work closely with counselors, case managers, and other community providers to help ensure clients receive the support and services they need.

Through my work, I have gained valuable experience communicating with individuals experiencing mental health challenges, substance use disorders, and difficult life circumstances. I understand the importance of making individuals and families feel comfortable, respected, and supported when seeking treatment. I also have experience managing multiple responsibilities, maintaining confidentiality, and working independently in a fast-paced environment.

I earned my Associate of Applied Science degree in Human Services from Hazard Community and Technical College in December 2025. I am currently pursuing my bachelor’s degree in Human Services and Counseling at Lindsey Wilson University, with an expected graduation date of May 2027. I also hold credentials as a CADC Associate I, Adult Peer Support Specialist, Family Peer Support Specialist, and Registered Alcohol and Drug Peer Support Specialist.

I am especially interested in this opportunity because I understand how important the admissions process is for individuals and families seeking behavioral health treatment. I would welcome the opportunity to use my experience in client engagement, intake assessments, and care coordination to help adolescents and their families connect with the services they need.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to helping others would benefit Adolescent Wellness Academy.
Sincerely, 
Wava Banks

Throughout my education, I have gained knowledge in mental health, substance use disorders, counseling theories, crisis intervention, ethics, case management, and treatment planning. I have also completed hands-on practicum experience in behavioral health, including observing clinical assessments, treatment planning, and counseling services.

In addition to my college education, I have earned certifications as an Adult Peer Support Specialist, Family Peer Support Specialist, Registered Alcohol and Drug Peer Support Specialist, and Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor Associate I (CADC-A I). I have also completed numerous professional trainings related to behavioral health, trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, crisis intervention, and substance use treatment.

My education, professional credentials, and hands-on experience have prepared me to work with individuals and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment services. I am committed to continuing my education and plan to pursue a master’s degree after completing my bachelor’s degree.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With my background in case management, behavioral health, administrative coordination, and supporting individuals experiencing substance use disorders and mental health challenges, I believe I would bring a unique combination of professional experience, compassion, and dedication to your admissions team. Helping individuals access the resources they need to begin their recovery journey is something I am genuinely passionate about.

Throughout my professional experience, I have worked with individuals facing serious and persistent mental illness, substance use disorders, and significant barriers to accessing healthcare and community resources. My background in case management and healthcare linkage has given me valuable experience coordinating services, supporting clients through difficult situations, maintaining confidential documentation, and helping individuals navigate complex systems. I have also worked with incarcerated populations, an experience that strengthened my commitment to reducing barriers to treatment and supporting individuals who are often overlooked.

In addition to my behavioral health background, my experience as an Administrative Assistant at Lattes on Location strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to coordinate multiple responsibilities while maintaining clear communication. My positions as a Registered Behavior Technician with Action Behavior Centers and Teacher Assistant with SESI Schools further developed my ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, adapt to individual needs, and remain calm and compassionate in challenging situations.

I recognize that reaching out for substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, not only for the individual seeking help but also for their loved ones. I believe the admissions process should be welcoming, informative, and free of judgment. My experience building rapport, communicating with individuals from diverse backgrounds, and coordinating care has prepared me to provide that level of support while ensuring timely follow-up and accurate documentation.

I am also pursuing my education in Addiction Studies, which reflects my long-term commitment to working with individuals affected by substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions. Principles Recovery Center's emphasis on individualized treatment aligns closely with my professional values and the type of meaningful work I hope to continue throughout my career.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, strong communication skills, and passion for addiction recovery to Principles Recovery Center. I look forward to discussing how I can contribute to your admissions team and help individuals take those important first steps toward recovery.

Sincerely,

Taylor Cowles-Kokofsky

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Principles Recovery Center Hiring Team,

I am incredibly excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. I have spent the last ten years in management and customer-facing roles, where I have learned that some of the most important work we do is helping people feel heard, understood, and supported during difficult moments. I am currently pursuing my undergraduate degree in Social Work because I want to build a career centered around mental health and helping others, and I would love the opportunity to bring my experience and passion to a team making a meaningful difference in people's lives.

Throughout my career, I have managed fast-paced operations, led teams of more than 25 employees, handled sensitive conversations, and helped people navigate stressful situations with patience and compassion. One thing I have learned is that people often reach out when they are overwhelmed, frustrated, or unsure of what to do next. My approach has always been to listen first, understand their concerns, and help them feel comfortable moving forward. I believe that ability to build trust is especially important when speaking with individuals and families who may be taking the difficult first step toward substance use or mental health treatment.

While my professional background has not been directly in substance use treatment admissions, I bring extensive experience in communication, organization, documentation, problem-solving, and managing multiple priorities independently. I am comfortable learning new systems and processes, following through on important details, and making sure people receive the information and support they need. I understand that the admissions process requires both compassion and consistency, and I would take seriously the responsibility of helping prospective clients navigate their options and connect with the appropriate next steps.

What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to combine the skills I have developed throughout my career with the field I am working toward professionally. I am eager to learn more about treatment admissions, PHP and IOP levels of care, and the systems your team uses to coordinate intakes and support prospective clients. I know I would bring a strong work ethic, a willingness to learn, genuine empathy, and the kind of follow-through that helps people feel supported rather than forgotten.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to Principles Recovery Center and support the important work your team does. I hope to have the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience, people skills, and commitment to mental health could make me a valuable addition to your team.

Warmly,  
Megan Olsen

Dear Hiring Team,
I am excited to apply for the Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. With an
Associate of Arts in Psychology and hands-on experience in sober-living program administration, applicant
intake, admissions coordination, and resident support, I bring a strong foundation in helping people navigate
recovery-related services with compassion, organization, and professionalism.
In my current role with House of Hope and Dreams, I coordinate approximately 15 applicant inquiries and

next steps, follow up on outstanding information, and coordinate admissions and resident transitions. I also
maintain confidential records, monitor compliance documentation, and support occupancy across a 30-bed
program. This work has strengthened my ability to communicate with people facing sensitive circumstances
while keeping processes organized and moving forward.
I understand that a responsive admissions process requires timely follow-up, accurate documentation, and
close coordination with other team members. My experience using RingCentral, Google Workspace, and
digital tracking tools has prepared me to manage communications and administrative workflows
independently in a remote environment. I would welcome the opportunity to build on my recovery-setting
experience while learning Principles Recovery Center’s specific procedures and systems.
I am drawn to PRC’s work supporting adults experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental
health conditions. I would be proud to contribute to a respectful, client-centered admissions experience that
helps individuals and families take the next step toward treatment.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my
background in applicant intake, program coordination, documentation, and recovery support could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Mikaela Whitney

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Psychology from Eastern Kentucky University, a Peer Support Specialist certification, and professional experience in behavioral health, case management, and substance-use recovery, I bring a strong foundation in compassionate client support, care coordination, and relationship building. I am also pursuing a Master of Social Work at Eastern Kentucky University as I continue working toward my long-term goal of becoming a licensed mental health professional.

During my time at Level Up Recovery and Isaiah House Treatment Center, I supported individuals navigating substance-use disorders, behavioral health challenges, and significant life transitions. My responsibilities included conducting client assessments, coordinating treatment and community resources, developing individualized service plans, maintaining confidential documentation, and helping clients overcome barriers to care. These experiences taught me the importance of patience, consistency, active listening, and meeting people where they are in their personal journeys.

I am particularly interested in Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its commitment to helping adolescents and their families access meaningful mental health support in a safe, structured, and compassionate environment. I understand that young people experiencing emotional or behavioral challenges need more than services alone; they need to feel heard, respected, and supported by people who recognize their individual strengths and circumstances. I would welcome the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate the intake process, coordinate appointments, communicate next steps, and remain engaged with their care.

In addition to my behavioral health background, my experience in court services and broadcast media has strengthened my organizational, communication, technical, and problem-solving skills. I am comfortable managing detailed records, coordinating multiple responsibilities, working with computer systems, and collaborating with professionals to ensure that important tasks are completed accurately and on time. I understand the importance of confidentiality, appropriate professional boundaries, and promptly communicating concerns to the appropriate clinical team members.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my education, professional experience, and commitment to person-centered care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am eager to contribute to a team that helps young people and their families feel less alone while connecting them with the support they need to move forward.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experience could contribute to your organization’s mission.

Sincerely,

Bradley Swafford

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Admissions Coordinator position at the Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over seven years of direct experience in behavioral health and substance use services — including hands-on admissions coordination across residential, Medical Withdrawal, and outpatient levels of care — I am confident I can step into this role and contribute immediately.

Early in my career at The Bridge Behavioral Health, I managed admissions across Civil Protective Custody, Medical Withdrawal, and Residential Treatment settings. I conducted initial screenings, gathered intake documentation, coordinated placement decisions with clinical staff, and educated individuals and their families on program options and expectations. That experience gave me a deep, practical understanding of the admissions process for adults in acute SUD and co-occurring crises — and the communication skills required to meet people with compassion at some of the most difficult moments of their lives.

At CenterPointe, I continued that work in a community-based setting, managing inbound inquiries, coordinating service eligibility, maintaining HIPAA-compliant case documentation in electronic systems, and collaborating with referral sources, prescribers, and clinical teams to resolve barriers and facilitate timely admissions. I'm comfortable independently managing an active pipeline, following up consistently with prospective clients, and maintaining the organized, accurate records that keep admissions operations running smoothly.

My background in a federally-funded substance use research study also sharpened my ability to engage individuals with SUD in sensitive conversations, track outreach activity across a caseload, and produce timely, accurate documentation in compliance with federal standards — skills I'd bring directly to managing PRC's admissions pipeline and CRM/EMR records.

I am drawn to the Adolescent Wellness Academy because of your commitment to accessible, high-quality SUD treatment. I would enjoy helping young adults find treatment options that are right for them and hopefully provide the intervention that could change their adult lives. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your census goals while supporting individuals and families in finding the care they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

I am eager to begin my career in this field by learning from experienced professionals while contributing my strong work ethic, organizational skills, and commitment to person-centered care.

My experience working within hospital systems and federally qualified health centers has also given me an appreciation for multidisciplinary teamwork, regulatory compliance, and the importance of providing services that are both compassionate and accountable. I am confident that my professional maturity, adaptability, and dedication to continuous learning will allow me to become a valuable member of your team.

I am seeking an organization where I can grow professionally, complete my clinical experience, and build a long-term career serving individuals and families affected by substance use and mental health challenges. Summer Balcaceres

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, graduate-level education in Clinical Psychology, and professional experience in substance use treatment, behavioral health intake, complex case management, and crisis intervention, I offer a strong combination of clinical knowledge, client engagement, and care coordination skills directly relevant to your admissions team.

My experience as a Sexual Trauma Advocate with Safe Passage has been particularly valuable in preparing me for this position. I worked with clients presenting with complex, overlapping needs, including sexual assault trauma, substance use concerns, psychiatric distress, and significant barriers to accessing treatment. My responsibilities included facilitating trauma-informed intake conversations, gathering sensitive client information, identifying immediate safety and psychosocial needs, and coordinating access to appropriate services. I supported clients requiring multifaceted care involving behavioral health providers, substance use treatment resources, medical services, and community support systems. My background at Metrolina Pain and Dependency further strengthened my familiarity with addiction treatment, particularly medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder. My experience supporting individuals with complex, interconnected treatment needs has prepared me to approach these responsibilities with sensitivity, efficiency, and professionalism.

I am confident in my ability to contribute to your admissions operations through effective client screening support, referral coordination, intake documentation, prospective client communication, and collaboration with clinical teams. HEATHER L. MARTINEZ
307-772-1172  |  heathermartinez07@gmail.com

October 16, 2026

Hiring Manager
Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Science in Healthcare Administration and a professional background in behavioral health, patient services, and administrative operations, I bring a strong foundation in compassionate communication and healthcare coordination. My experience includes assisting patients with intake documentation, verifying insurance eligibility, coordinating referrals, and maintaining confidential medical records. I understand the importance of creating a welcoming and supportive experience for individuals and families navigating challenging healthcare circumstances. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines my administrative strengths with my desire to help individuals access meaningful treatment and support.

During my medical front desk externship at the Depression and Bipolar Clinic, I supported daily clinical operations while interacting with patients experiencing behavioral health concerns. My responsibilities included coordinating appointments, processing new patient documentation, verifying insurance benefits, and communicating with clinical staff regarding referrals and patient needs. This experience strengthened my understanding of the sensitivity, discretion, and professionalism required when working with individuals seeking mental health services. Additionally, my background in financial services has further developed my ability to manage high volumes of inquiries, maintain accurate documentation, resolve concerns, and communicate effectively through telephone-based service platforms. These transferable skills would allow me to contribute to admissions coordination, prospective client follow-up, and efficient administrative workflows at Principles Recovery Center.

Throughout my professional career, I have consistently demonstrated strong organizational abilities, attention to detail, and a commitment to providing exceptional service. I am experienced in handling confidential information, managing competing priorities, and utilizing electronic systems to maintain accurate records and support daily operations. My familiarity with healthcare terminology, electronic medical records, HIPAA requirements, and insurance verification provides a foundation for learning the specific admissions processes associated with substance use treatment. I recognize that individuals seeking recovery services may be experiencing uncertainty, emotional distress, or significant personal challenges, making patience and compassionate communication essential throughout the admissions process. I would welcome the opportunity to apply my healthcare administration background while expanding my knowledge of substance use treatment programs and levels of care.

I am enthusiastic about the opportunity to contribute to Principles Recovery Center’s mission of helping individuals take meaningful steps toward recovery. I believe my combination of behavioral health exposure, administrative experience, customer service expertise, and dedication to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team. I am confident in my ability to work independently, maintain organized records, communicate professionally with prospective clients, and collaborate effectively with clinical and operational staff in a remote environment. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and transferable skills align with the needs of your organization. Thank you for your time, consideration, and the opportunity to apply for this meaningful position.

Sincerely,
Heather L. Martinez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
​I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background as a Certified Substance Abuse Counselor and a Police Dispatcher, I bring a unique combination of clinical assessment expertise, crisis evaluation, high-stakes communication, and detailed record-keeping. I am eager to leverage these skills to support families and young people navigating critical care transitions as part of your virtual admissions team.
​In my role as a Certified Substance Abuse Counselor, I gained extensive experience managing the end-to-end patient onboarding process. My core responsibilities included conducting thorough pre-admission assessments, facilitating the formal admission of new patients, maintaining detailed and compliant medical records, and delivering direct counseling. This clinical experience provided me with a deep understanding of behavioral health intake processes, compassionate family communication, and the importance of timely, precise documentation during critical stages of care.
​Prior to my work in counseling, I served as a Police Dispatcher, where I evaluated rapid, complex situations, coordinated emergency responses, and maintained accurate incident logs under high-pressure conditions. This experience sharpened my ability to manage high call volumes, multitask efficiently across digital platforms, exercise clear judgment, and remain calm, supportive, and reassuring during stressful human interactions—qualities essential for a remote admissions coordinator managing initial inquiries and intake calls.
​Joining Adolescent Wellness Academy appeals to me because of your commitment to guiding adolescents and their families toward healing and growth. I am confident that my blend of intake experience, clinical empathy, and calm crisis response will enable me to seamlessly guide prospective clients through the admissions process with care, efficiency, and professionalism.
​Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.
​Sincerely,
Christopher Maddocks

Hello, my name is Lindsey Vernarec and I am a people person. I have to ability to find a common ground with everyone, relate to them and make them feel comfortable in stressful situations. I can say with 100% confidence I work well with people, I make them feel like someone is on “their side” and advocating for them. I do not have direct mental health experience but working with the amount of patients I have, and the amount of customers/people, I have dealt with all walks of life in all different stages of life. I know how to be flexible and “read the room” to determine the best way to proceed with individuals and I am not afraid to ask them hard questions to understand their goals. My previous employer taught me “seek first to understand” and “everyone is wounded” meaning: you don’t know what a person is going through, them being irate or angry with you could be due to whatever they are experiencing, figure that out and understand that then proceed from there. 

I would be a worthy candidate for this role, I hope to speak to you and be able to demonstrate that. 

Thank you,
Lindsey Vernarec

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the position of Admissions Coordinator. I have 13 years of work experience as a Mental Health professional, server, sales associate, brand ambassador, dance teacher, and performer. Throughout these jobs, I have had the opportunity to develop a wide array of skills that I firmly believe make me the ideal fit for this position.

My work experiences have provided me the opportunity to hone important customer service and social skills. The most important skill I’ve learned, however, is maintaining a positive attitude. It may sound cliche, but just one smile can completely change someone’s day. Whether I was serving food and beverages to a table of customers, performing live dances for an audience, or teaching children, I strived to put a smile on someone’s face. I understand very well how isolation and disconnection have weakened human relationships. I want to strengthen those relationships and all it takes sometimes is a smile.

Throughout my 30 years, I have dealt with different mental illnesses that have brought me to where I am today. At 15, I was diagnosed with severe depression, anxiety, OCD, and ADHD. These challenges initially altered my ability to perform everyday tasks as well as school and dance. Today, after years of therapy, medication, and different psychiatrists, I am ready to support and give hope to others who have been given the same mental challenges I negotiated in my own life.

My diagnoses paired with my personality have made me a very empathetic, compassionate, and resilient person. Inspiring others (especially children and adolescents) through my story is my main goal in life. With my experience in Mental Health, customer service, and volunteer work, I’ve accumulated a unique skill set that would make me an asset for this position. I look forward to discussing my candidacy in more detail.

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Principles Recovery Center. With professional experience in mental health care, a Medical Assistant certification, and a deeply personal understanding of the impact substance use can have on individuals and families, I am passionate about helping people access the care and support they need to begin their recovery journey.

My experience in mental health care has strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, navigate sensitive situations, and recognize the importance of providing a supportive, nonjudgmental environment. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and genuine understanding. I would bring these values to every interaction with prospective clients and their loved ones.

Beyond my professional background, my connection to substance use treatment is deeply personal. Growing up with a close family member affected by substance use shaped my understanding of addiction and its impact on family dynamics, emotional well-being, and personal relationships. It also influenced my own relationship with alcohol, encouraging me to approach it with greater awareness, intentionality, and responsibility. These experiences have given me a unique perspective on the importance of recovery, the courage it takes to seek help, and the difference compassionate support can make.

What particularly draws me to Principles Recovery Center is the opportunity to serve as an initial point of contact for individuals seeking treatment. I recognize that the admissions process is more than scheduling appointments or completing paperwork. It is often someone’s first step toward changing their life. I would take that responsibility seriously, ensuring that prospective clients and families feel informed, supported, and respected throughout the process.

I am confident that my communication skills, attention to detail, ability to work independently, and commitment to mental health advocacy would allow me to contribute positively to your admissions team. Most importantly, I would bring a sincere dedication to helping individuals take meaningful steps toward recovery.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to further discuss how my professional background and personal experiences align with the mission and values of Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Alexia Davis

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals from a variety of backgrounds and across different stages of life, helping them navigate difficult situations, access resources, and take steps toward improving their overall well-being.

My experience as a Substance Abuse Counselor and Case Manager in an outpatient treatment setting has given me a strong understanding of the challenges individuals face when seeking treatment for substance use disorders. I have experience working with clients on treatment planning, documentation, care coordination, and connecting individuals with the services and support they need. I also have experience working in crisis settings, including mobile crisis and emergency room environments, which has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, remain calm under pressure, and respond to people with compassion and understanding.

In my role as a Veteran Peer Support Specialist, I further developed my ability to build rapport, listen without judgment, and help individuals feel comfortable discussing their needs and exploring their options. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be intimidating, and I believe the way someone is treated during that first interaction can make a real difference in whether they feel comfortable moving forward. I believe in meeting people where they are, helping them feel heard, and making the process as supportive and straightforward as possible.

Along with my hands-on experience, I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice and a Master of Arts in General Psychology. My education and professional background have given me a strong foundation in human behavior, mental health, substance use, documentation, and the importance of individualized support. I am comfortable working independently, managing responsibilities, maintaining accurate records, and communicating with individuals from diverse backgrounds.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and understanding of behavioral health and substance use treatment to your team. Helping others has always been important to me, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to a process that helps individuals take that first step toward recovery.

I am excited to apply for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a current Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) and college student pursuing my Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, I am passionate about working with children and adolescents and helping create an environment where they feel supported, respected, and encouraged to grow.

In my current role as an RBT, I work directly with children to support their behavioral, social, and communication goals. This experience has strengthened my ability to remain patient and calm in challenging situations, communicate effectively with children and families, follow individualized treatment plans, document progress, and collaborate with supervisors and team members. I have also learned the importance of building trust and creating positive relationships with the individuals I support.

I am particularly interested in Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its focus on supporting adolescents and their overall well-being. I would be excited to bring the skills I have developed through my RBT experience into a new environment while continuing to learn and grow professionally. I am comfortable receiving feedback, working as part of a team, and stepping into situations that require patience, empathy, and professionalism.

Alongside my professional experience, I am currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration. My education has helped me develop strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills that I believe would be valuable in a fast-paced healthcare and behavioral-health environment.

I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and passion for helping young people could contribute to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,

Savannah Crandall

**Hiring Manager**
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my background as a Registered Behavior Technician, my bachelor's degree in Clinical Psychology, and my experience working with children and families in behavioral health settings, I believe I would be a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role as a Registered Behavior Technician at Action Behavior Centers, I work closely with clients, families, clinicians, and interdisciplinary teams to support individualized treatment goals and promote positive outcomes. My responsibilities include maintaining accurate documentation, monitoring client progress, collaborating with clinical professionals, and communicating effectively with team members. These experiences have strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, professionalism, and ability to handle sensitive information while maintaining HIPAA compliance.

My educational background in Clinical Psychology, combined with my hands-on experience in behavioral health, has given me a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate, individualized care. I understand that seeking behavioral health services for an adolescent can be an emotional and sometimes overwhelming experience for families. I would welcome the opportunity to use my communication skills, empathy, and understanding of behavioral health services to help families navigate the admissions process and feel supported as they take the next steps toward care for their children.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my clinical experience in a role focused on connecting adolescents and their families with appropriate support and services. I am confident in my ability to remain organized, manage documentation accurately, communicate professionally in a virtual environment, and collaborate with team members to help ensure a positive admissions experience.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and passion for supporting children and families align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Sincerely,
**Kailah Cadena**

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. With over five years of experience in behavioral health administration, intake coordination, and client support, I bring a strong understanding of the admissions process, substance use treatment, and the importance of helping individuals and families navigate the path toward recovery.

In my work as an Intake Coordinator and Consultant with Transformative Health & Wellness, I have managed incoming inquiries, coordinated referrals, supported clients through the intake process, maintained accurate records, and collaborated with clinical teams to facilitate access to care. My experience working with behavioral health services, including IOP programs and substance use disorder treatment, has strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, assess client needs, and help individuals navigate treatment options and next steps.

I understand that the admissions process is often a critical first point of connection for individuals seeking treatment. I approach these conversations with empathy, professionalism, and a strong commitment to follow-through, recognizing that timely communication and consistent support can make a meaningful difference in whether someone accesses the care they need.

In addition to my direct intake and coordination experience, I am highly organized, comfortable managing multiple priorities independently, and experienced in tracking referrals, maintaining documentation, coordinating appointments, and supporting efficient administrative workflows. While I may not have worked with every specific platform listed in the posting, I have experience with comparable systems and am confident in my ability to learn new EMR and CRM software quickly while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality, and HIPAA compliance.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, strong communication skills, and dedication to client-centered care to Principles Recovery Center. I am especially interested in contributing to a team that helps individuals access meaningful treatment and supports them as they take important steps toward recovery.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Pilar

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 
	My name is Elizabeth (Lizzy) Shafer. I am a Colorado native from Pueblo and have lived in Colorado Springs for 7 years where I went to school to obtain a dual Bachelors degree in Psychology and Philosophy. I worked full time as well as went to school full time. I work amazing under pressure, in fact I thrive under it. I am looking to continue my education in psychology, preparing for an online masters program in the upcoming spring semester. I am looking to continue to grow my resume in the mental health field and find a job that fits well. I worked for a year as a Social Emotional Wellness Specialist at Harrison Highschool in Colorado Springs where I did casework, worked closely with the kids to monitor progression of behavioral and mental health issues, and helped with school work. I took on a caseworker role for a few months even without the licensure. I was the crisis navigator being the first call during a mental health crisis, and I was also a one on one para to kids and a tutor for many others. During this time I created very close relationships with many of the kids and I loved being able to help them and make a difference in their lives. Unfortunately, I did not wish to continue to work in a position with no clear instructions. It was the first year that this position was granted and it was apparent in how many shoes I was expected to fill with no clear direction. The staff was constantly praiseful, even now I will still receive messages from the staff asking for advice on how to deal with many of the kids that I formed a close relationship with. I loved the impact I made, but was looking for something more structured. 
	I see myself working with individuals who are suffering from a crisis. I deal very well with people who may not click with everyone else. I love to be able to find that human connection with people who have maybe struggled in the past. I have experience in casework, case management, crisis management, teamwork, substance abuse disorder, court systems, long term care plans, and connecting with individuals who may not have many people to help them. I am a team player and I am always able to take charge when needed, I find myself filling leadership positions constantly even when I do not desire to. I know whatever team I am a part of will always strive for success and work well together. I am excited to hear back and hopefully be a part of the team!
Warmest Regards,
Elizabeth Shafer

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

My professional background has taught me the importance of building trust, listening to individual needs, and helping people navigate important decisions. While my career has been rooted in sales, my passion has always been in mental health. I am eager to bring these transferable skills, along with my bachelor’s degree and personal commitment to mental health advocacy, to the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My own mental health journey has given me a deep appreciation for the impact compassionate, knowledgeable professionals can have on individuals and families during vulnerable moments. The empathy, validation, and support I have received have inspired me to pursue a career where I can offer that same sense of understanding to others. I am drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents and their families as they navigate the process of finding appropriate mental health treatment.

Throughout my sales career, I have developed strong communication, relationship-building, organization, and follow-up skills. I understand how important it is to listen carefully, establish rapport, respond thoughtfully to questions, and guide people through decisions that may feel overwhelming. I also recognize that admissions in a behavioral health setting requires more than coordination; it requires sensitivity, professionalism, discretion, and an understanding that reaching out for help can be a significant step for a family. I would approach every interaction with compassion while maintaining the organization, accountability, and attention to detail necessary to support an effective admissions process.

Although my professional experience has been in sales, my long-term goal is to build a meaningful career in mental health. I am currently studying for my Certification in Perinatal Mental Health Support (C-PMHS), further demonstrating my commitment to expanding my knowledge and contributing to the mental health field. I understand the importance of respecting professional boundaries, protecting confidential information, and helping individuals connect with appropriately qualified providers to meet their needs.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my relationship-management experience, strong work ethic, and genuine passion for mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Most importantly, I would bring a sincere commitment to helping adolescents and their families feel heard, supported, and respected as they take steps toward healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, transferable skills, and dedication to mental health can contribute to your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,
Nikki Marshall
